data.summary: This single‑week plan packs all eight units into a focused 12‑hour study block, starting with the weak Unit 4 and ending with a mixed review of key concepts. Each hour is dedicated to a concrete task that reinforces the week’s topic codes, ensuring the student covers every unit before the exam.

weeks.focus: Cover all units with a strong emphasis on Unit 4, then review and practice.
tasks: Do 15 practice problems on interpreting derivatives in context (4.1).
Solve 10 motion‑related problems using velocity and acceleration (4.2).
Complete 8 related‑rates problems covering non‑motion scenarios (4.4).
Review limit definitions and compute 10 limits algebraically (1.2).
Estimate 5 limits from graphs and tables (1.3,1.4).
Solve 10 algebraic limit problems (1.5).
Define the derivative and compute 10 basic derivatives (2.2).
Estimate 5 derivatives from graphs (2.3).
Show differentiability implies continuity on 5 functions (2.4).
Apply the power rule to 10 functions (2.5).
Use the chain rule on 8 composite functions (3.1).
Solve 6 implicit differentiation problems (3.2).
Differentiate 5 inverse functions (3.3).
Differentiate 4 inverse trigonometric functions (3.4).
Apply the Mean Value Theorem to 5 problems (5.1).
Use EVT to find extrema on 4 intervals (5.2).
Determine increasing/decreasing intervals for 5 functions (5.3).
Apply the first derivative test to 4 functions (5.4).
Approximate areas with Riemann sums for 3 functions (6.2).
Compute definite integrals using the Fundamental Theorem for 4 functions (6.4).
Model a simple differential equation and verify the solution (7.1,7.2).
Sketch slope fields for 2 equations and interpret (7.3,7.4).
Find average values of 3 functions over given intervals (8.1).
Integrate velocity to find position for 2 problems (8.2).
Use accumulation functions to solve 3 applied problems (8.3).
Find area between curves for 2 pairs of functions (8.4).
Take a full-length timed AP Calculus AB practice test.

data.final_week_advice: Use the final week to simulate exam conditions: complete a full timed practice test, then review all incorrect answers in detail, focusing on the concepts that caused mistakes. This will solidify your understanding and improve test‑taking strategy.
